measures: examples/cube as a player gets it: built for the web at --release with --define CUBE_PLAYER, which leaves its harness out; its wasm plus its JS, each at brotli quality 11, without the page shell or assets (tools/web-size.mjs). Each entry is a size the build had on the emcc it names, and why.

history.why: The cube enters with what it measures (kyoten's rendering.md § Decided, GFX-1's part 6, step 4, 2026-11-20): its player build, the harness left out by --define CUBE_PLAYER, with ENVIRONMENT=web. The goldens stay in it as assets, and emscripten's file packager with them, about 6.8 KB of the JS, since a build flag cannot leave a manifest's assets out (kyoten's KY-63): lower this with that reason when kama gives a way out. GFX-20 looks for what brings it under the hello cube's 150 KB gauge.

@kama/window's WIN-25 and WIN-26 (kama-window 642d116, 663689e and fedfc75), 564 B more: wasm 148,800 to 149,247 (its code 983 B larger before brotli, its data 64 B smaller), JS 20,291 to 20,408 (293 B larger before brotli). WIN-25 adds no code the cube keeps (its enums' serializers are pruned); alone it moved two trap sites' line numbers in window.kama, two bytes of a wasm of the same size, which brotli at quality 11 packs 163 B larger (measured by building against window.kama before and after it, kyoten's .scratch/s45/cubesize). The rest is WIN-26, each event's time, which kyoten's input needs: the event record 8 bytes longer, the C seam reading kama's clock and stamping each record, the web's times held to the pumps and in order, and the page reading each DOM event's timeStamp and a pad's timestamp.

kyoten's kama pin bump, 0.9.978 to 0.9.1018 (575a9cc6), with no source changed: 2,671 B more, wasm 149,247 to 151,951 (its code 11.5 KB larger before brotli, 481,824 to 493,599 B raw), JS 20,408 to 20,375. Measured by function in a --profiling-funcs build on each compiler (kyoten's .scratch/s45/bump/cubesize.sh): clang inlines kama's code differently, most of it into Cube.render (59.7 KB to 68.2 KB raw) as small helpers are folded into it (the vertex and settings writers putFloat, putWord, MaterialSettings.place and put, the Mat4 and Mat3 arrays' add), then NodeBuilder.spelled (+2.1 KB), Renderer.compileOn (+1.2 KB) and BufferGeometry.entryOn (+1.1 KB). kama's array growth route changed in that range (0.9.995 and 0.9.996: a capacity's bytes checked before any allocator is asked, KR-422), and DynamicArray's growTo is no longer a function of its own; its C emitter changed too, so the split between them is not measured. No feature added or dropped; GFX-20 looks for savings.

kyoten's kama pin bump, 0.9.1018 to 0.9.1026 (b2f627b0), with no source changed: 92 B more, wasm 151,951 to 152,043 (its code 291 B larger before brotli), JS 20,375 unchanged. Measured by function in a --profiling-funcs build on each compiler (kyoten's .scratch/s45/ready/cubesize26.sh): Cube.pumped alone grew (4,424 to 4,715 B raw), every other difference a renamed function of the same size. kama 0.9.1023 (KR-441) makes `cast<char>` trap on a value that is no Unicode scalar value, and @kama/window's eventOf, inlined into pumped, reads a text event's code point with one (`cast<char>(cast<uint32>(e.a))`); the new wasm carries that trap's message and the old does not. No feature added or dropped.
@kama/window WIN-27 (kama-window 9274a48): eventOf reads a Text event's code point with try cast<char>, so the cast's trap on a value that is no Unicode scalar value, and its message, leave the cube
